bias_confirmation.note: bias is a single global sampler value (motion_output_mode mip_bias=0.5), applied to every stage, not a light-map-stage-only value; this is the section-5 recommended A/B form, not the production stage-only form

method_caveat: Re-implemented from the note's description only (original scratchpad scripts are gone). Strip mask = HDR luma>0.8 AND depth valid (channel index 2 of depth_1 != -1) AND view_z in [5000,9500] units, a z-band proxy for the station, NOT the note's exact spar-box ROI (unrecoverable). Per-emitter forward tracking uses motion_1's (u,v,a) fields per tools/analysis/analyze_motion_readback.py's decode (dx=(u)*W-(px+0.5)) WITHOUT the per-frame jitter/raster-jitter correction that script applies; this is a known simplification.

sanity_check_failed.description: Re-running this session's tracker on the SAME run225 frames the note used does not reproduce the note's own numbers.
sanity_check_failed.conclusion: This session's per-emitter peak-ratio and frame-to-frame change numbers are NOT trustworthy (off by 4-5x from the note's own baseline, almost certainly a tracking/jitter-decode bug in the quick reimplementation, not a change in the scene). They are recorded below for completeness but should not be used for the verdict.

verdict.did_bias_change_strips: Modest, not decisive: horizontal 1-px run share dropped from 0.379 (bias -0.5) to 0.296-0.326 (bias +0.5) in both independent bursts, i.e. slightly fewer of the narrowest dashes / a small widening. Vertical 1-px share is unchanged in burst A (0.577 vs 0.566) and lower in burst B (0.504). Per-phase lit-pixel count and energy stayed within +-3.4% across phases in all three captures (jitter still moves energy between pixels, does not lose it), same as the note's finding, at both bias settings.
verdict.why_the_user_still_sees_no_help: The measured horizontal widening (about 15-20% relative drop in the narrowest-run share) is real but small, consistent with the note's mechanism: strips at this range have a coverage proxy far below 1 px (run225 median 0.76), so a 1-stop mip shift moves the sampled texel size but not far enough to cross the 1-px threshold; most dashes stay sub-pixel and keep tearing. The evidence rules out 'bias not reaching the light-map stage' as the reason (mip_bias=0.5 is a single global value, logged and applied to every stage including stage 2, confirmed above) -- so the remaining candidates from the note's Unknown section (aniso already integrating across the strip, or the selected mip already having a >=1px texel on this hull) are not distinguished by this A/B; both are still open per the note.
verdict.bearing_on_option_a_vs_b_prime: The small, inconsistent-in-direction effect (vertical axis) argues for the note's existing preference for option (a), a per-pixel analytic footprint, over further tuning of the per-stage mip bias: a full 1-stop global bias swing produced a sub-threshold change, so a stage-only bias (a strict subset of this A/B's effect) is very unlikely to do better. This session adds no new evidence against (a) and weak evidence that (b') alone will not resolve the symptom.
